subject: Sustained 429 sink-loop in production — HealthPort (urgent)
thread_summary: External report of rising 429s and timeouts. Root cause traced to org->project routing bug that funneled traffic into a low-capacity project causing quota exhaustion and a retry storm. Temporary mitigations (routing override and token-level throttles) applied; follow-up includes a config rollback and postmortem plan.

Subject: RE: 429s + timeouts across our ingestion pipelines (started ~06:50 PDT)

Team — short diagnosis from metrics: traffic shows correct origin tokens but wrong project mapping. An org->project aliasing regression in the tiering service caused a subset of HealthPort's high-throughput requests to be attributed to hp-ingest-staging-07 (which has a low project quota). When that project quota hit 100% the rate limiter started returning 429s; clients retried aggressively (backoff not sufficient) and created a feedback loop where retries further pushed the small project over quota.

Proposed immediate mitigations (I can action):
1) Temporarily whitelist HealthPort token(s) to bypass project quota and route to the parent org bucket for 30 minutes.
2) Apply a soft token-level throttle to cap client retry loops (burst=200/s -> 100/s).
3) In parallel, push a rollback of the latest tiering change (v3.12.4 -> v3.12.3) for the tiering service in the us-west-2 staging to stop further misattribution.

I recommend we do item 1 first (fastest) and 2 immediately after. Note: whitelisting will increase short-term cost but restores availability.

- Rafael
SRE Lead, Production Services
